thread_analysis.thread_summary: Pi Crystal Corporation (contacts Tomoko Suzuki, Junto Tsurumi) engages Allion (Kentaro Taniguchi, Itsuo Sakai) for Bluetooth SIG registration of a Nordic nRF52-series-based sensor device (WisSensor U-01), spanning March-April 2025. Beyond standard quote/Invoice/registration-completion administration, the thread surfaces a sophisticated and highly generalizable case about free derivative-product addition eligibility for third-party modules sharing the same chip family but different SDK/firmware lineages.
all_questions_found: Can a third-party module (BM832) referencing a different QDID/SDK lineage than the registration be added as a free derivative product, and how is this actually determined? (see thread_0054_case_01)

(Administrative, not separately cased) Standard new-customer onboarding (vendor information registration form, first-transaction prepayment requirement), Invoice/payment confirmation, Review Page confirmation and registration finalization, and standard Compliance Folder document checklist -- consistent with administrative content already documented extensively in other threads.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Case_01 is a valuable, previously undocumented extension of the free-derivative-addition concept: it clarifies that eligibility is determined by the actual SDK/firmware running on the device at deployment time, not by which QDID a module's factory datasheet or own pre-existing registration happens to reference -- and demonstrates the practical resolution pattern of confirming hardware/SDK compatibility directly with the module manufacturer when there's ambiguity.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0054_case_01 for the full decision logic.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See thread_0054_case_01; the risk cuts both ways -- assuming coverage based on chip-family similarity could result in an improperly scoped registration, while assuming non-coverage without checking actual firmware compatibility could result in an unnecessary full new registration.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: No significant consulting-side mistakes identified -- the consultant correctly identified the QDID lineage mismatch and provided the precise technical chain of reasoning (Declaration registration referencing a different SDK-based QDID with different Component-level registrations) when the customer's initial assumption was incorrect, then appropriately updated guidance once the customer obtained direct vendor confirmation.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When evaluating whether a third-party module qualifies for free derivative-product addition to an existing registration, trace the module's actual referenced QDID lineage (SDK version, Component-level registrations) rather than relying on chip-family similarity, and recommend the customer confirm actual SDK/firmware compatibility directly with the module manufacturer when the module's factory registration doesn't match the target registration's lineage -- since the determining factor is what firmware will actually run on the device, not what the module's original registration covers.
